transcript.text: This is Swift, an automated flood assistant working with local emergency services. Am I speaking with someone at 1868 Gretna Green Drive?
Yes, this is me. My wife’s recovering from surgery and can’t walk. Water’s already in the house.
I hear you're dealing with a flood and medical needs. How many people are at the home right now, including anyone who can't come to the phone?
Just me and my wife. She’s recovering from surgery and can’t walk.

I hear you’re staying with your wife. Is there anyone there who can't leave on their own, for example someone who uses a wheelchair, needs oxygen, or is bedbound? If it's a wheelchair, does it have a motor?
Yes, my wife can’t walk—she’s recovering from surgery. No wheelchair, motor or not.
I heard you, and I’m listening. Who is it that can't leave on their own, and what do they need to get out?
My wife, she’s recovering from surgery and can’t walk. She needs help getting out.
I hear you’re helping your wife get out safely. Is there water inside the home right now?
Yes, water’s inside. She can’t walk—need help getting her out.
I hear water’s inside and she can’t walk alone. If neighbors need a ride out, do you have a high-clearance truck, a boat, or free seats in a vehicle?
No truck, no boat, no seats. My wife can’t walk—she’s recovering from surgery.

I hear you’re caring for your wife right now. Let me read that back: 2 people; wife needs help leaving because of can't walk; wife needs help leaving because of help getting out; water is inside. Is that right?
Yes. Just me and my wife. She can’t walk, needs help getting out. Water’s inside. Can’t leave alone.

Acknowledged, you’re not alone in this. I've recorded that you need help leaving. No responder has been assigned yet. If water is rising inside, move to the highest floor and call 911 if you can get through. Goodbye.

house_card: Two people. Wife can’t walk. Water inside. English.
